text: system S species, \partial_t u_s - \nabla\cdot(D_s\nabla u_s) = R_s(u_1, \dots, u_S, x, t), \qquad s = 1, \dots, S, per-species diffusion, initial values boundary conditions.

title: Reaction-diffusion systems
text: reaction term uses product (group finite-element) approximation: R evaluated degrees freedom integrated M R(\mathbf U). exact linear reactions second-order accurate space smooth nonlinear ones, keeps reaction pointwise, Jacobians cheap. Two time integrators available: "imex-euler": (M + \Delta t K_s)\mathbf U_s^{n+1} = M(\mathbf U_s^n + \Delta t R_s(\mathbf U^n)); diffusion implicit, reaction explicit, species matrix factored . Stiff reactions need small steps. "implicit-euler": coupled nonlinear system (M_b + \Delta t K_b)\mathbf U^{n+1} - \Delta t M_b R(\mathbf U^{n+1}) = M_b \mathbf U^n solved Newton’s method backtracking line search. reaction Jacobian supplied user computed finite differences, one species time. Neither scheme guarantees positivity general reactions; check solution positivity matters.

title: Reaction-diffusion systems
text: Fisher-KPP equation \partial_t u = D\Delta u + r u(1 - u) develops traveling front speed 2\sqrt{rD}.  front position (u = 1/2) speeds toward asymptotic value 2\sqrt{0.1} \approx 0.63. Fronts start step data approach speed slowly , measured speeds little smaller:
code: mesh <- pde_mesh_rectangle(c(0, 10), c(0, 1), nx = 80, ny = 2) prob <- reaction_diffusion_problem(   mesh, species = "u", diffusion = 0.1,   reaction = function(u, x, y, t) u * (1 - u),   initial = list(u = function(x, y) as.numeric(x < 1)),   time = c(0, 12)) sol <- solve_pde(prob, dt = 0.1, method = "implicit-euler", output_times = c(0, 4, 8, 12)) summary(sol) #> Time-dependent finite-element solution #>   method: implicit-euler  dt:   0.1  steps: 120  #>   degrees of freedom: 243  ( 243  free) #>   linear solver: auto  max relative residual: 5.17e-16  #>   Newton iterations per step: max 3  mean     3  #>   integral of the solution, first and last stored time: 0.9375 to 7.069  #>   assembly 0.017 s, time stepping 0.859 s xs <- seq(0, 10, length.out = 300) plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 10), ylim = c(0, 1.05), xlab = "x", ylab = "u", main = "Fisher-KPP front") for (k in seq_along(sol$times)) {   lines(xs, evaluate(solution_at(sol, sol$times[k]), xs, rep(0.5, 300)), col = k, lwd = 2) } legend("topright", paste("t =", sol$times), col = seq_along(sol$times), lwd = 2, bty = "n") pos <- sapply(sol$times[-1], function(t) {   u <- evaluate(solution_at(sol, t), xs, rep(0.5, 300)); xs[which.min(abs(u - 0.5))] }) diff(pos) / 4 #> [1] 0.5769231 0.6270903

title: Waves and elastodynamics
text: wave_problem() poses  \partial_{tt} u + \gamma\,\partial_t u - \nabla\cdot(c^2\nabla u) = f(x, y, t)  initial displacement velocity usual boundary conditions, whose data may depend time. semidiscretization M\ddot{\mathbf u} + C\dot{\mathbf u} + K\mathbf u = \mathbf F(t) integrated Newmark average acceleration method (\beta = 1/4, \gamma_N = 1/2). second order unconditionally stable. Without damping forcing conserves discrete energy \tfrac12\dot{\mathbf u}^\top M\dot{\mathbf u} + \tfrac12\mathbf u^\top K\mathbf u exactly. effective matrix factorized . isolate time error, start discrete eigenmode K\mathbf x = \lambda_h M\mathbf x (computed solve_eigen()): semidiscrete solution exactly \cos(\sqrt{\lambda_h}\,t)\,\mathbf x, remaining error comes time stepping. relative energy drift rounding level. Damping removes energy:
